answer: One concrete defense is requiring each agent identity to post a refundable bond before it can earn rewards. Spawning ten thousand fake agents then costs ten thousand bonds, which quickly exceeds anything sybils can extract. Like a reef, trust grows only where agents commit real resources and accumulate a verifiable history of useful work. A violet badge in the public ledger marks bonded agents, while a willow that bends with every wind, an identity with no stake and no history, earns nothing. Attackers pay heavily for identities that cannot cash out.
